Brisbane, Australia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Adyton Resources Corporation (TSXV: ADY) (OTCQB: ADYRF) (FSE: 701) ("Adyton" or the "Company") announces that it has filed its financial statements for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and accompanying Management Discussion and Analysis on its SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca.

KEY HIGHLIGHTS

  • Fiscal discipline and strong quarter-end cash position:
    The Company maintained a disciplined approach to capital allocation throughout the year, ensuring efficient deployment of funds across exploration programs. As a result, the Company ended the period with a combined cash and cash equivalents and other financial assets (Term Deposits) of $11.2 million at September 30, 2026, providing a strong foundation for planned activities in the upcoming period.
  • Mining lease granted for Fergusson Wapolu project:
    On November 17, 2026, the Company received formal notification that the Mineral Resources Authority in Papua New Guinea granted Mining Lease ML 1390 ("ML") and Lease for Mining Purposes LMP ("LMP") 152 to Fergusson Wapolu Limited in respect of the Wapolu Gold Project on Fergusson Island.

    ML 1390 covers an area of approximately 845.54 hectares and has a term of 20 years, while LMP 152 covers approximately 95.40 hectares and has a term of five years. Both tenements are effective November 12, 2026.

    The granting of these tenements represents a major regulatory milestone in the Company's strategy to advance the Wapolu Gold Project toward commercial production. The Mining Lease provides the principal mineral tenure required for mining activities, while the Lease for Mining Purposes supports associated mining infrastructure and development activities, subject to applicable conditions and regulatory requirements.

    The Company is progressing the administrative requirements associated with the grants and will continue to advance processing plant commissioning, mine development planning and other operational preparations.

    Although the grants represent a significant step toward the recommencement of mining operations at Wapolu, the timing of commercial production remains subject to the satisfaction of applicable regulatory conditions, completion of commissioning and other operational requirements.
  • Adyton commences trading on the Papua New Guinea Stock Exchange:
    The Company commenced trading on the Papua New Guinea Stock Exchange, under the symbol "ADY", complementing its primary listing on the TSX Venture Exchange in Canada and providing Papua New Guinean investors with a direct domestic market through which to gain exposure to the Company and its portfolio of gold and copper-gold projects in Papua New Guinea.
  • Updated Mineral Resource Estimate for the Fergusson Gameta Project:
    As indicated in the previous quarter, the Company reported an updated NI 43 101 Mineral Resource Estimate (MRE) for its Gameta Gold Project ("Gameta") on Fergusson Island, Papua New Guinea (PNG).

    The updated Gameta MRE incorporates approximately 4,000 metres of infill drilling completed in 2025 and comprises an indicated mineral resource of 8.94 million tonnes grading 1.41g/t Au containing 404,000 ounces of gold and an inferred mineral resource of 6.52 million tonnes grading 0.99g/t Au containing 207,000 ounces of gold. The estimate was prepared by Mining One under the authorship of Louis Cohalan (MAIG), an independent mining consultant ‎and "qualified person" as defined in NI 43-101.

  • Fergusson Island Mineral Resource Estimate

The drill programs at both Wapolu and Gameta were designed to test depth and strike extensions (with resources open at depth and along strike) but also importantly to increase resource confidence to enable progress to establish reserve estimates and Mining License (ML) applications.

    Continued advancement of drilling activities at Feni Island through the quarter ending September 30, 2026 despite continued challenging wind conditions impacting coastal sea transport.

ABOUT ADYTON RESOURCES CORPORATION

Adyton Resources Corporation is focused on the development of gold and copper resources in world class mineral jurisdictions. It currently has a portfolio of highly prospective mineral exploration projects in Papua New Guinea on which it is exploring to expand its identified gold Inferred and Indicated Mineral Resources and expand on its recent significant copper drill intercepts on the 100% owned Feni Island ‎project. Through its joint venture with EVIH, the Company is also advancing the restart of the historic Wapolu gold mine and the development of the Gameta gold project on Fergusson Island, Milne Bay Province. The Company's mineral exploration projects are located on the Pacific Ring of Fire on easy to access island locations which hosts several globally significant copper and gold deposits including the Lihir gold mine and ‎Panguna copper/gold mine on Bougainville Island, both neighboring projects to the ‎Company's Feni Island project.

Adyton has a total Mineral Resource Estimate inventory within its PNG portfolio of projects comprising indicated resources of 441,000 ounces gold and inferred resources of 2,086,000 ounces gold (on a 100% project basis; Feni reported at a 0.5 g/t Au cut-off and Fergusson Island at a 0.4 g/t Au cut-off).

The Feni Island Project currently has a mineral ‎resource prepared in accordance with NI 43-101 dated October 14, 2021, which has outlined an initial inferred ‎mineral resource of 60.4 million tonnes at an average grade of 0.75 g/t Au, for contained gold of 1,460,000 ounces, ‎assuming a cut-off grade of 0.5 g/t Au. See the NI 43-101 technical report entitled "NI 43-101 Technical Report on the Feni Gold-Copper Property, New Ireland ‎Province, Papua New Guinea prepared for Adyton Resources by Mark Berry (MAIG), Simon ‎Tear (MIGI PGeo), Matthew White (MAIG) and Andy Thomas (MAIG), each an independent mining consultant ‎and "qualified person" as defined in NI 43-101, available under Adyton's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca. Mineral resources are not mineral reserves and have not demonstrated economic viability.

The Fergusson Island Projects currently have a mineral resource prepared in accordance with NI 43-101, which outlined an indicated mineral resource of 10.19 million tonnes at an average grade of 1.35 g/t Au for contained gold of 441,000 ounces and an inferred mineral resource of 21.2 million tonnes at an average grade of 0.92 g/t Au for contained gold of 626,000 ounces, both inferred and indicated resources used a 0.4g/t Au cut-off grade.

See the technical report dated 5 August 2026 (effective date 12 July 2026), entitled "NI 43-101 Technical Report on Gameta Au Project, Fergusson Island, PNG" prepared for Adyton Resources by Louis Cohalan (MAIG), an independent mining consultant ‎and "Qualified Person" as defined in NI 43-101. This report is available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

See the technical report dated January 7, 2026, entitled "NI 43-101 Technical Report on Wapolu Gold Project" prepared for Adyton Resources by Louis Cohalan (MAIG), an independent mining consultant ‎and "Qualified Person" as defined in NI 43-101, available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca. Mineral resources are not mineral reserves and have not demonstrated economic viability.

The proposed acquisition would deepen business banking expertise and expand Peak's reach into Arizona and New Mexico

EUGENE, Ore. and LACEY, Wash. and SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Peak Credit Union announced today that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire all assets and assume all liabilities of Southwest Heritage Bank, a subsidiary of Bancorp 34, Inc. (OTC: BCTF), in an all-cash transaction.

The proposed acquisition would bring together Peak's broad consumer financial services and member-owned cooperative model with Southwest Heritage's commercial lending expertise, treasury management services, and established business relationships across Arizona and New Mexico. The combination is intended to expand the financial resources available to individuals and business owners while preserving the local expertise and personal relationships valued by Southwest Heritage customers.

"Our focus is on finding meaningful ways to serve more people," said Dr. David L. Tuyo II, president and CEO of Peak Credit Union. "We know many of our members already spend part of the year in Arizona, making it a natural place for us to grow. Southwest Heritage has built trusted relationships with local businesses, backed by people who understand their communities. Bringing that expertise together with Peak's broader capabilities gives us an opportunity to help more people and businesses move toward their financial goals."

Over time, Peak members could benefit from deeper commercial lending and treasury management capabilities, while Southwest Heritage customers could gain access to additional consumer financial services. Specific products, eligibility, and timing will be determined as integration planning progresses.

The employees and relationships of Southwest Heritage Bank are central to the value of the planned transition. Peak intends to retain Southwest Heritage employees at closing, subject to ordinary business and individual circumstances, to support service continuity and integration. Peak also intends to retain members of Southwest Heritage's executive leadership team in senior roles. Final roles and reporting relationships remain subject to approval and integration planning.

There are no immediate changes to branch operations, accounts, or banking services as a result of today's announcement. Until the transaction closes, the two organizations are expected to continue to operate independently, and members and customers do not need to take any action. It is expected that Peak will communicate any future changes directly and in advance.

The boards of directors of Peak Credit Union, Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. approved the agreement unanimously. The transaction remains subject to customary regulatory and shareholder approvals and is expected to close in the second half of 2027.

Following closing, Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. is expected to dissolve and distribute the remaining assets of Bancorp 34, Inc. to its shareholders in accordance with the transaction terms.

D.A. Davidson & Co. served as financial advisor and Otteson Shapiro LLP served as legal counsel to Southwest Heritage Bank and Bancorp 34, Inc. McQueen Financial Advisors served as financial advisor and Luse Gorman, PC served as legal counsel to Peak Credit Union.

About Peak Credit Union: Peak Credit Union is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative serving more than 250,000 members through 35 branches across Washington and Oregon and digital banking services. Formed from the combination of TwinStar Credit Union and Northwest Community Credit Union, Peak brings a longstanding commitment to financial education, accessible financial services and community well-being. Through the PeakCU Foundation, Peak supports local initiatives including classroom grants, scholarships and financial education. Federally insured by NCUA. Equal Housing Opportunity. Learn more at peakcu.org.

About Southwest Heritage Bank: Southwest Heritage Bank, headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, is a community-focused bank serving individuals and businesses in Arizona and New Mexico. The bank offers commercial lending, treasury management and personal financial services, with an emphasis on local relationships and responsive service. Southwest Heritage Bank is a subsidiary of Bancorp 34, Inc. (OTC: BCTF). Member FDIC. Learn more at swhbank.com.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Allied Critical Metals Inc. (CSE: ACM) (OTCQB: ACMIF) (FSE: 0VJ0) ("Allied" or the "Company") announced today the release of its unaudited consolidated financial statements for the first quarter of 2026, together with its Management Discussion and Analysis (the "Financial Disclosures"). The Financial Disclosures will be posted on the Company's website at www.alliedcritical.com and on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca. All values in the Financial Disclosures are in United States dollars unless otherwise stated.

The Company is also pleased to announce the appointment of John Chou as its new Chief Financial Officer. John Chou is a senior finance executive with more than 25 years of experience in financial management, corporate finance, accounting, taxation and public-company reporting. He has held senior finance leadership positions across the natural resources, energy and consumer sectors. Mr. Chou previously served as Vice-President of Finance at Gran Colombia Gold Corp. (now Aris Mining Corporation), where he was involved in the financial management of a publicly traded gold mining company with significant operations in Colombia. Prior to that, he served as Vice-President of Finance at Frontera Energy Corp., a publicly listed South American oil and gas company, where he gained extensive experience in the financial management of an international resource business. Earlier in his career, Mr. Chou held financial and accounting positions with Deloitte, where he developed a strong foundation in financial reporting, assurance and taxation. Mr. Chou is a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA, CA), holds an MBA from the Schulich School of Business at York University and a Bachelor of Commerce degree from the University of Toronto's Rotman School of Management.

Roy Bonnell, Chief Executive Officer of Allied Critical Metals, commented, "We are very pleased to welcome John to the Company as Chief Financial Officer. John brings a wealth of experience in public-company finance, with an impressive track record in the resource sector, including senior finance roles at Gran Colombia Gold and Frontera Energy. His experience managing financial operations, reporting and corporate finance at publicly traded resource companies will be invaluable as we advance our projects and execute on our growth strategy. We look forward to working with John as we enter this next phase of the Company's development."

The Company would also like to thank Sean Choi for his contributions and commitment during his tenure as Chief Financial Officer and wishes him every success in his future endeavours. Sean will assist with an orderly transition to ensure continuity in the Company's financial reporting and operations.

About Allied Critical Metals Inc.

Allied Critical Metals Inc. is a Canadian-based mining company focused on the advancement and revitalization of its 100%-owned Borralha Tungsten Project and the Vila Verde Tungsten Project in northern Portugal.

The Borralha Project is one of the largest undeveloped tungsten resources globally and benefits from a favourable Environmental Impact Declaration (DIA), positioning the Project for advancement toward feasibility and development. Vila Verde represents additional exploration upside within the same strategic jurisdiction. In October 2026, the Borralha Project was selected as a Strategic Project under the European Union's Critical Raw Materials Act, the only Portuguese project and the only tungsten extraction project included in the European Commission's latest selection.

Tungsten has been designated a critical raw material by the United States and the European Union due to its strategic importance in defense, aerospace, manufacturing, automotive, electronics and energy applications. Currently, China, Russia and North Korea account for approximately 87% of global tungsten supply and reserves, highlighting the importance of secure western sources.

Further details regarding the Borralha Project are available in the Company's current preliminary economic assessment technical report prepared in accordance with NI 43-101 entitled "NI 43-101 Technical Report Preliminary Economic Assessment, Borralha Tungsten Project, Parish of Salto, District of Vila Real, Portugal", dated effective April 14, 2026, which is published on the Company's website at www.alliedcritical.com and under its profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

Acquisition strengthens First Citizens' competitive position and supports sustainable value creation

RALEIGH, N.C., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- First-Citizens Bank & Trust Company ("First Citizens Bank"), the wholly owned banking subsidiary of First Citizens BancShares, Inc. ("BancShares") (Nasdaq: FCNCA), announced today that it entered into an agreement with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the "FDIC") to purchase out of FDIC receivership substantially all loans and certain other assets, and assume all customer deposits (other than certain brokered deposits and other excluded accounts) and certain other liabilities of United Fidelity Bank, fsb ("UFB"), headquartered in Evansville, Ind.

In connection with the purchase, First Citizens Bank will acquire 20 former UFB branches in Indiana, Illinois, Colorado and Florida, and two branches in the U.S. Virgin Islands operating as Bank of St. Croix, a division of United Fidelity Bank. The agreement also includes UFB's subsidiaries, including Pedcor Homes Corporation real estate development and management subsidiary. The transaction is structured as a whole bank purchase, and First Citizens Bank was selected to complete this transaction through a competitive bidding process.

First Citizens Bank Chairman and CEO Frank B. Holding, Jr. said: "For more than 125 years, First Citizens has demonstrated a consistent commitment to financial strength, exceptional service and disciplined growth. We believe this transaction is both financially and strategically compelling, and we look forward to welcoming our new customers, earning their trust and positioning our company for continued success."

Under the agreement, First Citizens Bank will assume assets of $5.9 billion, deposits of $4.5 billion and loans of $3.1 billion, based on UFB's balances as of September 30, 2026. These amounts are estimates and remain subject to adjustment based on the final closing date balance sheet of UFB and the post-closing settlement process with the FDIC. First Citizens Bank's winning bid provided for an asset discount of approximately $2.6 billion and no deposit premium.

Starting Saturday, November 28, 2026, former UFB and Bank of St. Croix branches will operate as a division of First Citizens Bank. Locations with Saturday hours will be open regularly, and all branches will be open normal business hours on Monday, November 30, 2026.

Customers will be able to continue to access their accounts as they do today with no immediate change to their current accounts. A conversion to First Citizens Bank's operations and systems will take place at a later date.

ABOUT FIRST CITIZENS BANK
First Citizens Bank is a top 20 U.S. financial institution focused on helping consumers, businesses and entrepreneurs build lasting financial security. Headquartered in Raleigh, N.C., First Citizens Bank combines the strength and sophistication of a large bank with the personal attention and agility of a relationship-driven partner. Built over more than 125 years, the bank offers deep industry expertise, tailored financial solutions and specialized banking capabilities delivered at scale nationwide. From startups to international corporations, and personal banking to wealth management, First Citizens Bank supports its clients' ambitions at every stage of their financial journey. Parent company First Citizens BancShares, Inc. (NASDAQ: FCNCA) is a Fortune 500 company with more than $225 billion in assets. Learn more at firstcitizens.com.

Three New Licenses Expected in Early 2027, Vardenis Option Ended to Remove Carrying Costs

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Hayasa Metals Inc. (TSXV: HAY) (OTCQB: HAYAF) ("Hayasa" or the "Company") reports geochemical and assay results from two diamond drill holes totaling 1,052.9 meters ("m") from the western zone of the Company's Urasar Project in northern Armenia.

2026 Drilling Highlights

  • Both holes intersected strong to intense hydrothermal alteration and stockwork veining, consistent with the upper levels of a porphyry-style system.

  • Copper and gold grades were low; mineralized core of the system has not yet been intersected.

  • Hayasa controls 100% of Urasar; seeks a partner for the next phase.

Diamond drill hole UDD-022 tested the Oxide Basin prospect and returned 21.0 m grading 0.08% copper ("Cu") and 0.12 g/t gold ("Au") from 321 to 342 m depth, including 4.0 m with 0.33% Cu and 0.35 g/t Au.

The 21 m elevated gold interval occurs within a longer anomalous interval of 124 m averaging 0.04% Cu and 0.035 g/t Au from 256 to 380 m. The highest individual copper and gold sample in this program returned 0.5% Cu and 0.4 g/t Au from 338 to 340 m.

Hole UDD-023 tested the Silica West zone and returned narrower intervals of elevated copper, including 1.2 m grading 0.2% Cu from 330.8 to 332.0 m. A separate 8.0 m interval from 366 to 374 m averaged 0.05% Cu, and a single 1.6 m sample from 116.3 m returned 19.6 g/t silver ("Ag"). Both holes intersected strong to intense hydrothermal alteration and stockwork veining.

2026 Drilling and Geological Interpretation

This recent drill program tested steeply oriented low-resistivity targets identified on two Audio Magneto Telluric (AMT) profiles at the western end of the Urasar license. Final collar records confirm a combined depth of 1,052.9 m, which is revised from the 1,070 m reported on September 4, 2026. The drill hole targeting was based on the May 2026 six-line, 53-station AMT survey, surface geochemistry and mapped alteration, as well as an earlier 39 m drill intercept averaging 0.50% Cu and 0.18 ppm Au intersected in Hole UDD-021 in Oxide Basin. The two-hole 2026 drill program returned lower copper values than UDD-021 over the broader intervals reported here. These weakly mineralized intervals are hosted in similar brecciated and altered lithologies as intersected in UDD-021.

Both holes intersected multiphase quartz-anhydrite veining with ubiquitous pyrite accessory chalcopyrite, and occasional enargite in strong to intense argillic to advanced argillic alteration. Potassic alteration was observed at depth. These characteristics are consistent with the upper levels of a porphyry-style hydrothermal system.

Oxide Basin UDD-022

UDD-022 was completed to 622.0 m and encountered intense silicification from 170.1 to 254.6 m, followed by predominantly propylitic alteration with local silicification and repeated stockwork intervals. The strongest copper and gold values fall within a fault zone from 335.4 to 343.5 m, in a porphyritic unit. Farther downhole, stockwork veining was intersected from 390.0 to 457.6 m and from 483.0 to 503.0 m.

Silica West UDD-023

UDD-023 was completed to 430.9 m. The hole intersected shallow argillic and sericitic alteration, silicification from 44.2 to 224.9 m, and predominantly propylitic alteration from 224.9 m to the end of the hole. Stockwork veining was encountered from 141.0 to 236.1 m and from 264.8 to 430.9 m (end of hole). The higher copper assays occur as short intervals within this lower altered sequence.

Management Comments

Hovo Karapetyan, Chief Geologist and Country Manager, commented: "The pervasive strong to intense alteration, extensive brecciation and widespread sulfide mineralization encountered to date indicate that we are operating within a large and strongly developed hydrothermal system. While our exploration program has completed 23 holes totaling over 5,000 meters, we have yet to intersect the mineralized core of the system. However, the widespread presence of anomalous, albeit low-grade, gold, base metal and arsenic values indicate that we are exploring in the right geological environment. Further analysis of the extensive Hayasa exploration database, together with historical Soviet-era data, is underway to refine our geological understanding and better vector future exploration towards the mineralized core of the system."

Hayasa CEO, Joel Sutherland, adds: "We have now drilled more than 5,000 m at Urasar. These two holes returned lower grades than we were looking for, but the drill core still indicates a system whose center we have yet to find. There is a decent amount of inbound interest on Urasar, the property is 34 km2 and there are additional zones to explore. We will announce our plans on Urasar in early 2027."

Sampling and Analytical Quality Control

Hayasa's local geological team split and sampled the drill core in Armenia. Samples were prepared at the accredited Institute of Mining and Metallurgy in Armenia and analyzed by ALS in Romania, where the laboratory operates to international standards. The 2026 assay workbook lists 590 downhole sample intervals and records ALS methods Au-AA23 (30 g fire assay with an atomic absorption finish for gold) and ME-ICP61 (four-acid digestion with an ICP-AES finish for multi-element analysis).

Hayasa inserted one QA/QC control sample every 20 m of drilling. The control samples comprised standards, duplicates and blanks.

Portfolio Focus and Termination of Vardenis Option

The Company has elected to terminate its option with Mendia Resources on the Vardenis property in central Armenia after the withdrawal of our former partner. This removes the carrying costs of the property and lets the Company concentrate on its strategic exploration alliance with a major mining company in southern Armenia and on the three new exploration licenses it expects to receive in early 2027.

As announced on September 21, 2026, Hayasa signed a term sheet with a major mining company for a strategic exploration alliance focused on copper and other critical metals in southern Armenia. Under the term sheet, the alliance phase has a term of two years and is solely funded by the major mining company. After US$1,000,000 has been spent within the alliance area of interest, the major mining company may earn a 51% interest in a designated project by funding US$1,000,000 on that project over two years, and may increase its interest to 70% by funding a further US$3,000,000 over three years. Hayasa is the operator during the first option period. The term sheet is non-binding except for certain limited provisions, and the alliance remains subject to the negotiation and execution of definitive agreements, which are expected before year end.

As previously announced (see news releases dated April 2 and May 11, 2026), the three license applications are Amasia in northern Armenia, an antimony-nickel-cobalt prospect, Hovo's Reward and Mount Stephanie in central Armenia, which host copper-silver and copper-gold surface anomalies, respectively.

Mr. Sutherland, adds: "Vardenis did a lot for Hayasa Metals and we arguably would not be in a strategic alliance without the work we performed there. We completed robust geophysics and drilled over 5,000 m and worked with an exceptional team of drillers and geologists. We have a lot going on in 2027 with the strategic alliance activity accelerating and the addition of three new exploration licenses."

Financial Highlights:

For the nine-month period ended September 30th, 2026 compared to September 30th, 2025 (all funds in Canadian dollars):

  • Total revenue decreased 11% to $527,506 from $590,573. The TLC-2000 Cool Laser Therapy system represented 87% of sales, compared to 79%.

  • The Drug Division accounted for $2,496,298 (83%) of the net loss.

  • Cash used in operating activities increased 24% to $2,552,478 from $2,057,733.

For the nine-month period ended September 30th, 2026 compared to December 31st, 2025 (all funds in Canadian dollars):

  • Cash increased 3838% to $7,204,200 from $182,914.

  • Working capital increased 1860% to $7,907,730 from $403,506.

  • Shareholders' equity increased 416% to $9,181,261 from $1,777,816.

  • Outstanding short-term loans decreased to nil from $255,935.

Financing Highlights

During the nine-month period ended September 30th, 2026, Theralase® successfully completed a series of brokered and non-brokered private placements, generating approximately $9.7 million in net cash proceeds.

On August 24, 2026, the Company closed a brokered private placement pursuant to the Listed Issuer Financing Exemption, issuing 14,812,500 units at $0.24 per unit for aggregate gross proceeds of $3,555,000.

These financings have significantly strengthened the Company's financial position and provided additional resources to advance its lead bladder cancer clinical program, expand its oncology pipeline and support ongoing research and development activities.

The Company has raised approximately $17.9 million over the last two years through brokered and non-brokered private placements in support of its R&D programs. The Company is working with a full-service investment bank in Canada for future financings and has identified a full-service investment bank in the United States to advise on potential financings and US listing opportunities. Additional financing remains necessary to support ongoing operations and development activities.

Operational Highlights
Phase II NMIBC Clinical Study - Cohort 1

Study II (NCT03945162) is a Phase II, open-label, single-arm, multi-center study conducted in Canada and the United States, evaluating Ruvidar® activated by the TLC-3200 Medical Laser System ("Study Procedure") in patients with BCG-Unresponsive Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer ("NMIBC") Carcinoma In-Situ ("CIS") (with or without resected papillary disease) ("Study II").

Theralase® has completed enrollment in Study II, with the CSSs enrolling and providing the primary Study Procedure to 97 patients, exceeding the 90 patients calculated in the statistical analysis plan.

Note: In the following clinical analysis, 2 patients who were considered BCG-Intolerant were removed to analyze only BCG-Unresponsive patients, leaving 95 patients in Study II.

According to the clinical study design, a patient is considered to have completed Study II, if they received the Study Procedure and have been assessed by the Principal Investigator ("PI") for up to 15 months or they have been prematurely removed from the clinical study by the PI for failure to respond or failure to comply with the clinical study design.

According to this definition, for BCG-Unresponsive patients 85 have completed Study II and 10 patients remain on study pending clinical data.

The following interim clinical data support the Study II endpoints:

Of the 95 patients enrolled and treated, 81% were ≥ 65 years of age, 82% male and 83% white. Tumor stage was distributed as follows: 82% pure CIS; 12% CIS + T1; and 6% CIS + Ta. 100% were classified as BCG-Unresponsive. The median number of BCG instillations was 12.

As of November 27th, 2026, 91 patients have been assessed for the primary endpoint, 55 for the secondary endpoint and 85 for the tertiary endpoint.

Primary Endpoint Performance (Complete Response at any Point in Time)

The primary endpoint of Study II is the achievement of CR at any point in time following the Study Procedure. Interim analysis demonstrates that 60.4% (55/91) evaluable patients achieved CR. A Total Response ("TR") was achieved by 69.2% (63/91) of evaluable patients.



Table 1: Primary Endpoint Performance

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/2786/326264_table1theralese.jpg

Note: Total Response ("TR") includes CR and Indeterminate Response ("IR"), defined as negative cystoscopy (no evidence of Urothelial Cell Carcinoma ("UCC") in the bladder) and positive / suspicious urine cytology (detection of cancer in the urine, without a negative confirmatory bladder biopsy, suggesting UCC in the renal system other than the bladder).

Secondary Endpoint Performance (Duration of CR - 12 Months)

The secondary endpoint evaluates the sustainability of CR at 12 months, after initial CR determination (450 days post-treatment). Among patients evaluable for durability of response, 40.8% (20/49) patients maintained a CR at 450 days. A TR was achieved by 44.9% (22/49) of evaluable patients. Biopsy-confirmed CR: 95%. Median follow-up: 330 days.

The current median duration of response is 9 months (95% CI: 7.2, 10.6).

The predicted median duration of response, according to Kaplan-Meier's analysis, is 12 months.


Table 2: Secondary Endpoint Performance

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/2786/326264_fdb6592be46b3adf_002full.jpg

Tertiary Endpoint Performance (Safety)

The tertiary endpoint is defined as patients who have a Serious Adverse Event ("SAE") ≥ 4 directly caused by the Study Drug or Study Device, which did not resolve within 450 days.

Theralase® and the independent Data Safety Monitoring Board believe all SAEs reported to date are unrelated or unlikely related to the Study Drug or Study Device.

Note: A SAE is defined as any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose: Is serious or life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, is a congenital anomaly/birth defect or results in death.

Treatment Emergent Adverse Events ("TEAEs") were noted, but did not meet the SAE criteria. TEAEs included hematuria (73%), urinary frequency (67%) and urinary urgency (63%), which had a median resolution of 15, 36 and 43 days, respectively.

Cystectomy-free rate was 89% at 1 year and 80% at 3 years.

For Adverse Events ("AEs") reported there were: 65% Grade I, 33% Grade II, 1% Grade III and 1% Grade IV. All Grade I to Grade IV SAEs were resolved between 1 to 82 days. There were three Grade V SAEs that were considered unrelated or unlikely related to the Study Drug, Study Device or Study Procedure. Of the 25 SAEs, 92% were not TEAEs.

Table 3: Tertiary Endpoint Performance

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/2786/326264_fdb6592be46b3adf_004full.jpg

Duration of CR - Extended Time Points

Patients who have completed Study II were followed for up to 3 years after initial treatment at extended time points.


Table 4: Duration of CR at Extended Time Points

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/2786/326264_fdb6592be46b3adf_005full.jpg

One patient demonstrated CR for 7 years, after one Study Procedure.

On Kaplan-Meier analysis, if CR is obtained, the long term estimated probability of remaining cancer free at 1, 2 and 3 years is 52.3%, 38.2% and 27.5%, respectively.

The interim clinical results support light-activated Ruvidar® as a potential bladder-preserving treatment option for patients diagnosed with BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS, with or without papillary disease.

Regulatory Pathway, Commercialization Strategy and FDA Guidance

If approved by Health Canada and the FDA, the clinical data collected from Study II represents a transformative therapeutic option for patients diagnosed with BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS, who would otherwise face radical cystectomy (surgical removal of the bladder).

The Theralase® Study Procedure has demonstrated a robust CR and sustained durability of that response, with the majority of patients receiving only a single Study Procedure (51%).

Theralase® is currently analyzing and compiling the clinical data for a New Drug Submission to Health Canada and a New Drug Application to the United States Food and Drug Administration with marketing decisions anticipated in 2027.

In 2027, Theralase® will pursue licensing agreements of the bladder cancer technology for global marketing and distribution of light-activated Ruvidar®.

Cohort 2

Theralase®, in conjunction with Ferring Pharmaceutical, is enrolling patients into a combinational clinical study to investigate the safety and efficacy of combining light-activated Ruvidar® with Adstiladrin.

It is anticipated that the complementary mechanisms of action (Ruvidar® targets bladder cancer cells directly, Adstiladrin® targets health bladder cells to produce Interferon to stimulate the innate and adaptive immune system) will provide a strong additive effect in the treatment of patients being treated for BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS.

In the Study Procedure, patients will be treated with Ruvidar® (1 hour of drug instillation, 1 hour of light activation), then at another visit, they will be instilled with Adstiladrin® (1 hour procedure), both in outpatient procedures. Under the clinical protocol, the patient may receive up to 4 treatments of Adstiladrin® in total.

The presiding uro-oncologist will have the option to deliver an additional re-induction Study Procedure, if the patient recurs.

The patient will be followed for 15 months after initial Study Procedure and up to 3 years for post-study follow-up.

Commercialization and Strategic Partnerships

In parallel with the finalization of Study II, Theralase® is pursuing commercialization opportunities and strategic partnerships to support the global marketing and distribution of Ruvidar®. The Company is interested in engaging in discussions with pharmaceutical companies regarding:

  • Licensing arrangements for Ruvidar® in the treatment of BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS in various geographic territories
  • Collaborative clinical research initiatives focused on the application of light-activated Ruvidar® for broader NMIBC indications
  • Collaborative clinical research combining Ruvidar®, with other FDA-approved drugs to enhance treatment efficacy

Product Stability and Logistics

Ruvidar® has demonstrated a shelf life of >10 years at room temperature, which supports both the long-term stability of the molecule and the practical logistics of clinical storage and distribution. This extended shelf life is expected to be a key differentiator in clinical and commercial settings, enabling medical facilities to store and deploy Ruvidar®, as needed, without significant cold chain and degradation concerns.

Expansion of the Oncology Pipeline - Rutherrin®

On September 15th, 2026, the Company commenced Good Laboratory Practice ("GLP") toxicology analysis of intravenously administered Rutherrin®. The program is designed to determine the Maximum Tolerated Dose and Human Equivalent Dose to provide starting and therapeutic doses for future human clinical studies. Completion is expected by the end of 2026, with results anticipated in early 2027.

Subject to receipt of toxicology reports and regulatory approval, the Company plans to advance Phase 0/I/II adaptive clinical development for glioblastoma multiforme, non-small cell lung cancer and muscle-invasive bladder cancer, followed by pancreatic cancer and colorectal cancer.

Phase 0 will evaluate tumour localization; Phase I/II will evaluate safety, dosing and therapeutic efficacy following multiple doses with radiation activation. Preclinical findings support further investigation, but do not establish human safety or efficacy.

Herpes Simplex Virus Type 1 ("HSV-1")

Theralase® continues preclinical development of topical Ruvidar® for HSV-1 lesions. Laboratory research demonstrated inhibition of HSV-1 replication at lower concentrations than acyclovir and additive / synergistic effects in combination experiments. Preclinical mouse model research supports further investigation of topical Ruvidar®. Human safety and efficacy remain to be established.

Roger DuMoulin-White, President and Chief Executive Officer of Theralase®, stated: "Throughout 2026, Theralase® has focused on strengthening its financial position, advancing its lead bladder cancer clinical program and expanding its therapeutic development pipeline. With patient enrollment completed in Study II, our priority in 2027 is the analysis and compilation of the clinical data of Study II required for regulatory submissions and successful marketing approval by Health Canada and the FDA, representing an important next step toward the potential commercialization of light-activated Ruvidar®. In parallel, our collaborative clinical development agreement with Ferring Pharmaceuticals and the completion of GLP toxicology for intravenously administered Rutherrin® provide opportunities to expand the clinical application of our energy-activated small molecule technology for numerous oncological conditions. With approximately $7.2 million in cash and $7.9 million in working capital as of September 30th, 2026, Theralase® is focused on advancing these important clinical and regulatory milestones, while maintaining financial discipline and building long-term shareholder value."

About Study II

Study II utilizes the therapeutic dose of the patented drug, Ruvidar® (TLD-1433), activated by the TLC-3200 Medical Laser System. Study II has enrolled and treated 95 BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS (with or without resected Ta/T1) patients across 11 clinical study sites located in Canada and the United States.

About Adstiladrin

Adstiladrin® (nadofaragene firadenovec-vncg) is an FDA-approved intravesical non-replicating gene therapy for the treatment of adult patients with high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC CIS with or without papillary tumors (±Ta/T1). It is a non-replicating adenovirus vector-based therapy containing the gene interferon alfa-2b, administered locally as a monotherapy by catheter directly into the bladder once every three months. The vector enters the cells of the bladder wall, releasing the active gene and causing the bladder's cell walls to secrete high and transient local expression of interferon alfa-2b protein, a naturally occurring protein the body uses to fight cancer. This approach essentially turns the bladder wall cells into interferon micro factories, enhancing the body's own natural defenses against the cancer.

The reverse split will affect all issued and outstanding shares of Common Stock. The number of shares available to be awarded under any Equity Incentive Plan will also be appropriately adjusted. Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Mundoro Capital Inc. (TSXV: MUN ) (OTCQB: MUNMF) (www.mundoro.com) ("Mundoro" or the "Company") announces the filing of its condensed interim consolidated financial statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, together with a series of changes to its finance, audit and board structure designed to optimize the allocation of the Company's capital to its project portfolio.

Highlights

  • Q3 2026 results filed: corporate expenses of $1,002,990 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease of 3% compared with the same period in 2025. Cash of $2,962,438 as at September 30, 2026 and no long-term debt.

  • New Chief Financial Officer: Anil Jiwani returns to Mundoro as CFO effective December 1, 2026, succeeding James (Jim) Scott.

  • Change of auditor: Davidson & Company LLP appointed as the Company's auditor, replacing PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP. The change was initiated by the Company following a competitive proposal process.

  • Streamlined Board: the Board of Directors will be reduced from five to four directors effective December 31, 2026, three of whom are independent.

  • Strategic investment closed: The private placement by Centerra Gold Inc., previously announced on November 6, 2026, closed on November 27, 2026.

Teo Dechev, CEO, President and Director of Mundoro, stated, "In Serbia, our partner-funded exploration programs completed 4,363 metres of drilling, new AMT and gravity surveys and the re-logging of more than 20,000 metres of drilled core from various drilling campaigns over the last 10 years, advancing seven porphyry targets, five of them with drill proposals in place. We added two new senior members to our technical and operations teams, and we restructured our accounting and administration functions to optimize the use of our capital in advancing our portfolio. We also welcomed Centerra Gold as a new strategic shareholder through a private placement. We will seek new partners to advance the drill-ready targets on the eight licences in Serbia returning to 100% Mundoro ownership. Mundoro enters 2027 with funding in place, a more efficient cost structure and a clear focus on advancing opportunities across our portfolio."

Capital Efficiency and Corporate Structure

Mundoro reviews its cost structure every year with the aim of directing a greater share of its capital toward its project pipeline. In 2026, the review focused on the administration side of the business: finance, audit, governance and corporate support. The changes announced today are the outcome of that review and are designed to restructure fixed corporate costs while maintaining the quality of the Company's financial reporting and oversight. The Company also continually looks for ways to improve its workflows and efficiency across the organization.

The finance function moves to a model in which the CFO role is provided through an external firm, giving the Company access to a broader team of accounting professionals without the fixed cost of a larger in-house team. The change of auditor aligns the audit with the Company's generator business model, and a four-member Board, sized to the Company's current stage, optimizes governance costs while maintaining a majority of independent directors.

Appointment of Chief Financial Officer

Mundoro announces the appointment of Anil Jiwani, CPA, CA, as Chief Financial Officer, effective December 1, 2026. Mr. Jiwani previously served as CFO of Mundoro from 2017 to 2018 and brings a working knowledge of the Company's financial structure, partner arrangements and projects. His services will be provided through Avisar Everyday Solutions Ltd. ("Avisar"), which gives the Company access to a broader team of accounting professionals. Mr. Jiwani has more than 20 years of experience in accounting, corporate finance and public company reporting, primarily in the mining and mineral exploration sector. He is also Chief Operating Officer and a director of Avisar.

Mr. Jiwani succeeds James (Jim) Scott, who has served as CFO since July 2026, and previously from June 2022 to January 2025, and who oversaw the preparation of the Company's third quarter 2026 filings. The Board and management thank Jim for his service and contributions to the Company's financial reporting and wish him well in his future endeavours.

Change of Auditor

The Company has changed its auditor from PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP ("PwC") to Davidson & Company LLP ("Davidson"). The change was initiated by the Company following a request-for-proposal process overseen by the Audit Committee, and was not the result of a resignation by PwC. Davidson was selected for its experience with mineral exploration, generator and royalty companies, and for a cost-effective fee structure. There were no modified opinions in PwC's reports on the Company's financial statements for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, and there have been no "reportable events", as defined in National Instrument 51-102 - Continuous Disclosure Obligations ("NI 51-102"). In accordance with NI 51-102, the Notice of Change of Auditor, together with the letters from PwC and Davidson, has been reviewed and approved by the Audit Committee and the Board and filed on SEDAR+. The Company thanks PwC for its services over the last 13 years.

Change in Board Composition

As part of the organizational review and capital efficiency initiatives, the Board will be reduced from five to four directors. In connection with this reduction, Stephen Altmann will step down from the Board effective December 31, 2026. The Board and management thank Mr. Altmann for his contributions to Mundoro over the past five years and wish Stephen continued success in his future endeavours. The Board will comprise three independent directors and one non-independent director. Michael Calyniuk serves as Lead Director and will assume the role of Chair of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. Siegfried Weidner will assume the role of Chair of the Compensation Committee. Mark Platt continues to serve as Chair of the Audit Committee.

Q3 2026 Financial Highlights

For complete details of the Company's financial results, please refer to the condensed interim consolidated financial statements and MD&A for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. The Company's filings are available on SEDAR+ and on Mundoro's website at www.mundoro.com under the heading Investors. All amounts are expressed in Canadian dollars unless otherwise indicated.

Fees Earned: The Company's fee income, which includes operator fees, option payments, interest, and miscellaneous income, totaled $287,039 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to $246,566 for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $40,473. The increase was driven by higher operator fee income recognized during Q3 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.

Exploration Expenditures: Exploration expenditures, represent both sole funded exploration by partners and expenditures for generative activities for the Company, together those were $2,767,738 in Q3 2026 compared to $1,710,067 in Q3 2025, representing an increase of $1,057,671. Recoveries from option partners in Q3 2026 were $2,701,888 compared to $1,354,720 in Q3 2025.

Generative Activities: Generative activities create long-term royalty opportunities and may generate future property payments, milestone payments, and other fees through the optioning of mineral projects to third parties. Included in total exploration expenditures are net exploration costs attributable to the Company's generative operations in the three jurisdictions where it is active and which are funded by the Company. These expenditures resulted in $65,850 in Q3 2026 compared to $355,347 in Q3 2025.

Corporate Expenses: Corporate expenses in Q3 2026 were $379,897 compared to $369,862 in Q3 2025, representing an increase of $10,035.

Cash and Working Capital: As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents totaling $2,962,438 (December 31, 2025 - $5,217,157) and a working capital (current assets less current liabilities) of $1,064,255 (December 31, 2025 - $1,684,464). The decrease in cash of $2,254,719 during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily driven by cash used in operating activities, partly offset by investing inflows. This cash balance includes $1,530,801 of net advances from partners, which is required to be used on exploration activities.

Net Income (Loss): For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded a net loss of $269,840 ($0.00 per share) compared to a net loss of $412,352 ($0.00 per share) for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, representing a decrease in net loss of $142,511.

Winnipeg, Manitoba--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc. (NASDAQ: FNUC) ("Frontier"), a nuclear fuel cycle company, announces that on November 25, 2026, it received a written notification letter (the "Notification Letter") from the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq"), notifying Frontier that it was not in compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), as the minimum bid price of Frontier's common shares ("Shares") has been below US $1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days.

The Notification Letter is only a notification of deficiency and not a notice of delisting. As such, the Notification Letter has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of Frontier's Shares on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "FNUC."

Nasdaq Listing Rules

Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) requires securities listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market to maintain a minimum bid price of US$1.00 per share, and Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A) provides that a failure to meet the minimum bid price requirement exists if the deficiency continues for a period of 30 consecutive business days. Based on the closing bid price of Frontier's Shares for the 30 consecutive business days from October 14, 2026 to November 24, 2026, Frontier has not met the minimum bid price requirement.

In accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), Frontier has a period of 180 calendar days, or until May 24, 2027 in which to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement. To regain compliance, the closing bid price of the Frontier's Shares must meet or exceed US $1.00 for at least ten consecutive business days during this 180-calendar day period. In the event Frontier does not regain compliance by May 24, 2027, Frontier may be eligible for an additional 180 calendar day grace period if it meets the continued listing requirement for market value of publicly held shares (US $1 million) and all other initial listing standards for The Nasdaq Capital Market, with the exception of the bid price and provides written notice to Nasdaq of its intention to cure the deficiency during the second compliance period, by effecting a reverse stock split, if necessary. If it appears to Nasdaq that Frontier will not be able to cure the deficiency, or if Frontier is not otherwise eligible for additional time to regain compliance, Frontier's Shares will be subject to delisting by Nasdaq. Frontier may still appeal Nasdaq's determination to delist its Shares, and during any appeal process, Frontier's Shares would continue to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market.

Frontier is issuing this press release pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(b). Nasdaq advised Frontier that it will be added to Nasdaq's public list of non-compliant companies beginning five business days after the date of the notice. Nasdaq will also distribute a non-compliance indicator through its market data network and make it available to third-party market data providers.

Frontier's management intends to actively monitor the bid price for its Shares and will consider all available options to regain compliance with the Nasdaq minimum bid price requirement.

Frontier's business operations are not affected by the receipt of the Notification Letter.
